articles.title: Twins, Sonny Gray agree to deal reportedly for 2 years and worth $55 million with an opt-out
articles.summary: Gray returns to Minnesota, where he spent the 2022 and 2023 seasons.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Twins and starting pitcher Sonny Gray have agreed to a deal.

The team confirmed the signing Wednesday on social media, and ESPN's Jeff Passan reported that the deal is a two-year, $55 million contract with an opt-out after the first year.

Gray returns to Minnesota, where he spent the 2022 and 2023 seasons. In his previous stint with the Twins, Gray started 56 games over two seasons, tallying a 16-13 record and a 2.90 ERA.

The 37-year-old spent last season with the Boston Red Sox where he made 29 starts and finished with a career-high 18 wins. Gray went 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA and struck out 149 batters in 169 innings.

His wins and ERA were Boston's best last season. Gray's 18 wins were tied with Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sánchez and Arizona Diamondbacks southpaw Eduardo Rodríguez for most in MLB last season. The veteran right-hander's 2.72 ERA was the eighth-best in all of baseball.

Minnesota has plenty of time to make more moves, but for now Gray looks to bolster a 2027 rotation consisting of Joe Ryan, Pablo López, Dean Kremer and Taj Bradley. López missed all of last season due to Tommy John surgery, but is expected to be ready toward the start of next season, pending a lockout.

This is the Twins' second deal this offseason. Minnesota extended a qualifying offer to catcher Ryan Jeffers. The catcher accepted it and will earn $23.15 million next season with the Twins.
